title: The City After Dark
text:
Descriptions of urban life tend to assume a daytime citizen: someone who shops, works and uses public services while the sun is up. Yet a considerable part of the city depends on people whose working day begins when the conventional one ends.

For cleaners, hospital staff and delivery workers, reduced transport services are not a minor inconvenience. They influence which jobs are accessible, how much unpaid time a shift requires, and whether the journey home feels reasonably safe.

Planning for the night therefore involves more than promoting entertainment. A lively restaurant district may coexist with poorly lit routes used by workers leaving its kitchens. Measuring nightlife through spending alone leaves these experiences largely invisible.

A more inclusive approach would ask whose needs disappear when services close, and who absorbs the resulting costs. Treating the night as an ordinary part of civic life changes the question from how to attract visitors to how to support the people already there.
textTranslate:
对城市生活的描述往往预设了一类白天活动的市民：他们在太阳升起时购物、工作并使用公共服务。然而，城市中相当大的一部分运转，依赖于那些在常规工作日结束时才开始上班的人。

对清洁工、医护人员和配送人员而言，公共交通班次减少并不是小小的不便。它影响哪些工作可以接受、一班工作需要付出多少无薪时间，以及回家途中能否感到基本安全。

因此，夜间规划不仅仅是促进娱乐消费。热闹的餐饮街区，可能与后厨工作人员离店时经过的昏暗道路同时存在。如果只用消费金额衡量夜生活，这些体验在很大程度上就会被忽视。

更具包容性的方式，是追问服务关闭后谁的需求消失在视野之外，以及由谁承担由此产生的成本。把夜间视为公共生活的正常组成部分，会使问题从“如何吸引访客”转向“如何支持已经在这里的人”。

title: The Value of Expert Doubt
text:
Expertise is frequently associated with the ability to answer quickly. In public debate, hesitation can look like weakness, while an unqualified prediction attracts attention. The incentives of the conversation may therefore reward precisely the behaviour that careful investigation tries to avoid.

An experienced specialist often knows not only what the evidence supports, but also where it becomes thin. Distinguishing a reliable conclusion from a plausible interpretation requires sensitivity to methods, missing information and the limits of transferring results between contexts.

This does not mean that every opinion deserves equal weight or that action must wait for certainty. It means that the confidence attached to a claim should be part of the claim itself. An estimate accompanied by clear conditions can be more useful than a dramatic promise.

The challenge is institutional as well as personal. If organisations punish revised judgements, experts learn to conceal uncertainty. When updating a position is treated as evidence of responsible reasoning, doubt can become a resource for better decisions rather than an obstacle to authority.
textTranslate:
专业能力常被理解为迅速给出答案的能力。在公共讨论中，犹豫可能显得软弱，而毫无保留的预测更容易吸引注意。因此，讨论中的激励机制可能恰好奖励了审慎研究试图避免的行为。

有经验的专业人士通常既知道证据支持什么，也知道证据在哪些地方变得薄弱。要区分可靠结论和看似合理的解释，需要敏锐地认识研究方法、缺失信息，以及把结果移用于不同情境时的局限。

这并不意味着每种意见都应获得同等分量，也不意味着必须等到完全确定后才能行动。它意味着，一项主张的可信程度应该成为主张本身的一部分。附带明确条件的估计，可能比夸张的承诺更有用。

这既是个人挑战，也是制度挑战。如果组织惩罚经过修正的判断，专家就会学会掩饰不确定性。当更新立场被视为负责任推理的表现时，怀疑就能成为改善决策的资源，而不再只是权威的障碍。

title: The Price of Convenience
text:
Convenience is usually presented as a personal benefit: fewer steps, shorter waits and less effort. What disappears from this account is the work transferred elsewhere. A seamless experience for one person may depend on fragmented schedules and constant availability for another.

Consider a service that promises delivery at almost any hour. Its appeal is easy to understand, especially for people with limited mobility or demanding responsibilities. Yet the promise also shapes expectations, making a reasonable delay appear to be a failure rather than a normal constraint.

Assessing such services requires resisting a simple opposition between progress and nostalgia. The relevant question is how benefits and burdens are distributed, and whether the people carrying the burdens have meaningful influence over the conditions of their work.

Convenience need not be rejected to be examined. Making its hidden arrangements visible allows users, workers and providers to negotiate a different balance, one in which saved minutes do not automatically justify every demand made in their name.
textTranslate:
便利通常被描述为个人收益：步骤更少、等待更短、付出更小。这种叙述忽略了被转移到别处的工作。一个人的顺畅体验，可能依赖于另一个人被切割的工作时间和随时待命的状态。

想想一种承诺几乎任何时间都能送货的服务。它的吸引力不难理解，尤其对行动不便或承担繁重责任的人而言。然而，这种承诺也塑造了预期，使合理的延迟显得像一次失败，而不是正常限制。

评估这类服务，需要避免简单地把进步与怀旧对立起来。真正相关的问题是，收益和负担如何分配，以及承担负担的人能否对自身的工作条件施加实质影响。

审视便利，并不需要先拒绝便利。让它背后的安排显现出来，才能使用户、劳动者和服务提供者协商出另一种平衡，让节省下来的几分钟不再自动成为一切要求的正当理由。

title: Translation as Interpretation
text:
A translation is often judged by how closely it follows an original, as though meaning were a fixed object that could be carried intact between languages. In practice, translators must continually decide which relationships matter most: tone, rhythm, precision or the social distance between speakers.

A perfectly ordinary form of address in one language may sound unusually intimate in another. Preserving the words can therefore alter the relationship they express. Conversely, changing the wording may be the most faithful way to reproduce the effect of the exchange.

These decisions are especially visible in humour, but they are not confined to literature. Instructions, public notices and workplace messages all rely on assumptions about what readers already know and how directly they expect to be addressed.

Recognising translation as interpretation does not make accuracy irrelevant. It makes the grounds of accuracy more demanding. A responsible translator should be able to explain what a choice preserves, what it sacrifices, and why that balance serves the reader in this particular context.
textTranslate:
人们评价译文时，常常看它与原文有多接近，仿佛意义是一件固定的物品，可以完整无损地在语言之间搬运。实际上，译者必须不断判断哪些关系最重要：语气、节奏、精确程度，还是说话者之间的社会距离。

一种语言中十分普通的称呼，在另一种语言里可能显得异常亲密。因此，保留字面措辞反而可能改变它所表达的关系。相反，改变措辞可能才是最忠实地再现交流效果的办法。

这些选择在幽默表达中尤其明显，但并不局限于文学。操作说明、公共告示和工作消息，都依赖一些假设：读者已经知道什么，以及他们期望别人以多么直接的方式对自己说话。

承认翻译也是诠释，并不会让准确性变得无关紧要，反而会对准确性的依据提出更高要求。负责任的译者应当能够解释，一种选择保留了什么、牺牲了什么，以及这种平衡为什么适合特定情境中的读者。
